rec.name: Image with Slides (Synced Image + Content Carousel)
rec.status: Built — launched (bug fix delivered; documentation in Slite)

what.text: A custom Shopify section ('CRO | Image with Slides') that pairs a rotated two-image collage with a text panel (subheading, large heading, body text). Round prev/next arrow buttons switch to the next slide. The image slides and text slides are two Swiper carousels kept in sync, so one click changes both. Each slide holds up to two images (a single image is also supported). The image side can sit left or right of the text. In the theme editor, a basic preview appears in the section picker.

why.text: Splits a brand, feature or benefit story into short, scannable chapters instead of one long text block. The visual + text pairing, and the arrows' sense of progression, invite interaction and keep attention on the value propositions. Showing several benefits in one compact spot saves vertical space and lets the page convey more USPs without long scrolling. The tilted, overlapping images add a more premium, editorial feel. Conversion impact is indirect; this is a storytelling and engagement element, not a direct purchase driver.

how.text: Create the section file 'ed-cro-multiple-image-with-slides.liquid' and paste the provided code. The section needs Swiper to be available in the theme (the code calls `new Swiper` but does not load it). Add 'slide' blocks, each with subheading, heading, text, and thumbnail 1 and 2. The code renders two Swiper instances (a content swiper and a media swiper) with fade effect and loop. They are linked via `controller.control`, so one arrow click syncs both. Instances are scoped by `section.id`, so the section can be added multiple times on a page and each slider works independently. This fixes the earlier bug where arrows showed the same pictures. The Shopify design-mode event `shopify:section:load` re-initialises the sliders in the theme editor. Spacing, sizes and colors are driven by CSS variables set from the section settings, with separate mobile and desktop values (breakpoint 1000px). One caveat from comments: the code file contains 'Step 1' twice, which may be a documentation error. Another: the arrow selectors `.contentSwiper_next/prev` are not scoped by section ID, which could cause cross-talk with multiple instances (my inference from the code).

items: Text color and background color (transparent default falls back to theme settings)
Section spacing top/bottom/left/right (desktop) plus separate mobile values
Thumbnail width (%) and thumbnail corner radius
Subheading, heading and body text sizes (desktop/mobile)
Arrow colors, border and background (default and hover/active state)
Slide blocks: subheading, heading, content text, thumbnail 1, thumbnail 2

Ticket asks for more (button text/link, price, alignment, vertical alignment, section height, background image/opacity). These are not visible in the provided code, so it is unclear whether they were built.

dependencies.text: Swiper JS library must be loaded in the theme (not included in the section code). Built for Shopify themes such as 'Impact' and 'Concept' (reference designs). Uses theme global settings 'text_color' and 'background' as fallbacks. Needs product/brand images for each slide (a comment notes a placeholder product image was still needed for both mobile and desktop). No metafields required.

items: Interaction rate with arrows (clicks per session)
Click-through to PDP/collection from the page
Add-to-cart rate / conversion rate vs. control
Bounce rate on the landing page

Reference from the 'Concept' theme: full-height image left, icon, heading and body text on the right.
Final built section on a white background: two tilted rounded images, subheading 'What we do', heading, body text, and round prev/next arrows.
Section picker in the theme customizer showing 'CRO | Image with Slides' with a basic preview (two placeholder images, text and arrows).
Built section ('About us' slide) with annotation reporting the arrow-navigation bug where pictures did not change. Fixed afterwards by scoping swipers per section.
